summary: Designed, implemented, and verified the Rust bitboard Drop7 engine and fair expectimax search: a 28-byte column-major nibble-packed board (gravity as a single PEXT bit-gather, row rise as (word << 4) | SOLID, board-wide cover-hit counting with a 4-way bitboard parallel counter), a statically dispatched pluggable leaf, and a measured-driven cheap direct-mapped depth-preferred transposition table. Proven bit-identical to the frozen C++ reference, the C++ fast engine, and the TypeScript engine across three trajectory drivers, 150,854 leaf bit-patterns, and d4s7/d5s7 per-column search values. Benchmarked against the TypeScript, C++ reference, and C++ fast engines with game-level thread scaling to 32 workers.
validationPerformed: cargo test: 14/14 unit tests pass (board packing, gravity, rise, mirror, scan, RNG, wave scores).
Trajectory gates: 0 mismatches over 512 center-policy + 256 search-policy games vs C++ playHeadlessMove and 256 games vs the TypeScript seededRandom driver (36,427 moves, 40,286 waves total).
Leaf gate: 150,854 real states bit-identical to C++ fastFairLeaf as uint64 patterns.

Search gates: 105 d4s7 roots (no-table and depth-gated arms) and 10 d5s7 roots with bit-identical per-column values and identical actions; values gate re-run with the table enabled proves cache-independence.
Search metrics gate: identical chosen action and completed depth to the C++ FastSearch on 105 d4s7 roots.
npm test 137/137 pass; make research-validate OK; web next build compiles and the approach page renders (HTTP 200).
make research-doctor machine profile captured to runs/RUN-20260824T052018Z-b88c3e22/rust-engine/machine-profile.json.
limitations: Self-reported contribution; not yet independently reviewed.
The runtime exposes the exact model identifier moonshotai/Kimi-K3 (baseten/moonshotai/Kimi-K3); reported as given.
Timing figures were measured on a shared workstation (load average 1.1-1.7); ratios between back-to-back arms are the trustworthy quantity.

The transposition-table design was revised during the work: an initial full strict-LRU port was removed at the owner's direction, and the shipped cheap direct-mapped table was then driven by the measured work-reduction data (1.3% node hit rate but 47%/90% work elimination at d4s7/d5s7).
No commit SHA: the work is uncommitted in the working tree at record time.
